citations.claim: initial total energy is 330 J with ball at rest at height 11
energy just below limit immediately before bounce
first violation: energy 368.34 exceeds allowed 368.0 at step 785

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 1/30 to 0.001 (only dt changed), same 785 steps: energy stays ~330.35 J with no violation, showing gain is numerical integration error at large dt

explanation: Single elastic ball bouncing on floor with max dt=1/30 and gravity=30 steadily gains energy: semi-implicit Euler adds ~0.05J per bounce via positional-correction / impulse ordering, accumulating from 330J to 368.34J by step 785 and breaching the 10%+5J bound. Smaller dt removes the gain.
vision_note: The single blue ball falls downward across steps 782 to 784 and reaches the floor by step 785. There is no visible tunneling, escape, or explosion, just a normal-looking bounce on the floor.
